correctness.rationale: Independently embed R^3 into R^4 by taking dot products with (+++),(+--),(-+-),(--+). This is an l1-to-linf isometry onto the hyperplane with coordinate sum zero. If the vertex coordinate ranges are [l_i,u_i], a fitting center at radius r exists exactly when each interval [u_i-r,l_i+r] is nonempty and their product meets the hyperplane, i.e. the sum of lowers is <=0<= the sum of uppers. This verifies the exact opposite-pair and parity bounds without assuming the list of dual extreme points. Each nonempty column subset sum occurs as an edge in some ordering; integrality gives a width cutoff of 2 below 3/2 and 3 at 3/2, with parity-sum cutoffs of 5 and 6 respectively. An independent bounded sweep tested three orders per frame, the other three being central reflections of these tetrahedra in the packet midpoint. Below 3/2 there were 24 necessary independent candidates, all index 2, and none fit; the unit frame fits the radius-3/2 cube ball. At 3/2 the prefilter yielded 512/408/288/56 candidates at indices 1/2/3/4, and 512/408/0/8 passed. The separate orbit regeneration matched all 23 CSV rows including sizes and representatives. Replay: python3 -I /workspace/branches/independent-checks/record2.py; output at /workspace/branches/independent-checks/record2.log. Original checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Exact exhaustion is for unordered independent integer frames with separate fitting centers, not arbitrary lattices, simultaneous common centers, or ordinary lattice covering radii.
